clue.text: Answer regularly appears — in case of multichoice — to be A?

definitions.note: A is the symbol for the unit, hence the question mark

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the casing taken from the following word
regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of multichoice

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the first and last letters of the word are wanted

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of appears

explanation.surface: A quiz-setter musing that the answer in a multiple-choice question tends to come out as option A.
explanation.walkthrough: AMPERE is A followed by M(PER)E. The definition is the single letter A, which is the SI symbol for the unit of electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere, the base unit of electric current, is written with the symbol A in physics and engineering.

clue.text: Agree to turn over mushroom

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing over another can cover it, here wrapping around it

parts.note: a turn is a stage act, as in a music-hall turn
a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: Consenting to flip a mushroom in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' looks like a reversal instruction, but turn is the noun and over places it around the mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept is to consent or say yes to something, so it is a verb synonym for agree.

clue.text: Drive for PC monitor maybe buggy

parts.note: to patrol is one way to monitor an area
a buggy is a small car

explanation.surface: Computer advice: a drive to go with your PC, though the monitor may have bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: PC, drive, monitor and buggy all suggest computing; PC is a police constable, and the drive is a vehicle he drives.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol car is the vehicle a police constable drives on duty, hence a drive for a PC.

clue.text: Available following press launch

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first word's letters go after the second's

parts.note: to roll is to press flat, as with a rolling pin
something out is on sale and available

explanation.surface: A product now on sale after its press launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press launch' looks like one phrase for a media event; the definition is launch alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the official introduction of a new product or service, which is a launch.

clue.text: Fit handle having shed and loft to keep it in

indicators.note: keeping something in means holding it inside, so the loft word goes around the rest

parts.note: a loft is an attic, the room under the roof

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so the following word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A DIY tip: if a handle has come off a shed, store it up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like the garden building the handle came off, but it works as a verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone athletic is in good physical condition, so fit is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Instruction to make 21 relax — have a break

definitions.meaning: 21 Across is TEASE; removing T, for time, leaves a word meaning relax
second meaning: to take a holiday or rest from work

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic instruction: TEASE minus T (time) gives EASE, which means relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as a literal command to remove the letter for time and as an idiom for taking leave.

clue.text: In just seconds, Blackpool rock always blackens kids' teeth — useless sticky sweets!

indicators.note: seconds here means the second letter of each word, and only those are used

parts.words: Blackpool rock always blackens kids' teeth — useless
parts.note: the second letter of each of these seven words

explanation.surface: A rant that Blackpool rock rots children's teeth in no time, calling sticky sweets pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool rock is a hard stick of seaside candy sold at the English resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollies are lollipops, sweets on a stick, which are sticky to eat.

clue.text: Name of singer Lorde's covering

parts.note: a tit is a songbird

indicators.note: a covering is the outside layer, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Lorde

explanation.surface: Asking the name of a cover version by the New Zealand singer Lorde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' points at Lorde but is a bird; 'covering' looks like a cover song.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name of a book, song or film, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Reason prisoner died breaking into 1 Down, for example

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: 1 Down is a clue in this very puzzle
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A convict reasoning out why someone died after a break-in.
explanation.walkthrough: CON + CLU(D)E. '1 Down' is not the answer ACCEPT but the clue itself, an example of a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude is to arrive at a judgement by logic, which is what reasoning does.

clue.text: Hereford and Gloucester, possibly about 7-1

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the minus sign between the two clue numbers means one thing is taken away from the other

parts.note: the answer to 7 Down
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A racing tipster quoting odds of 7-1 on Hereford and Gloucester.
explanation.walkthrough: 7-1 is not betting odds: it means TITLE minus I. Hereford and Gloucester look like cathedral cities or horses but are British cattle breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford and Gloucester are both breeds of cattle, so together they are examples of the answer.

clue.text: Having discounted a Japanese drink, reveal it's reduced to lowest strength

indicators.note: to discount something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the drink

parts.note: sake is Japanese rice wine
taken as written, then removed
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Someone who skipped the sake finally admits their drinking has dropped to its weakest.
explanation.walkthrough: SAKE without A leaves SKE, then LET ON. 'Strength' suggests drink but means the number of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton staff or crew is the bare minimum number of people needed to keep things running.

clue.text: Rugby player with a collection of books for supporter

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
a means one
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A rugby forward with a library becomes an advocate of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent argues in favour of an idea, so the word is a synonym of one who backs it.

clue.text: Boost in space with Solo from Star Wars bonding …

parts.note: an en is a printer's space
Han Solo is the smuggler in Star Wars
cement is a bonding agent

explanation.surface: Han Solo getting a lift in outer space while bonding with his crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Space here is not outer space but the printers' en, half an em wide.
explanation.definitionFit: An enhancement is an improvement or increase, so the noun boost is a synonym.

clue.text: Provide Aldi sandwiches — perfect

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold between, so the two words hold the letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the supermarket chain Aldi should sell sandwiches, which would be just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is flawless or exactly as wished, a direct adjective synonym for perfect.

clue.text: Made a good impression and occasionally ground out test match when playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about and rearranged
occasionally means only now and then, so just every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of the two words read together
taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman who impressed by grinding out a test match draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground out' sounds like a cricketer's dogged innings; it only supplies alternate letters. A test match is an international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for reaching the required standard, so it fits someone who impressed.

clue.text: … over a drink — wanting nothing under a gallon and getting mean

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means following it in the answer
wanting means lacking, so the letter for nothing goes missing

parts.note: taken as written, the a in 'under a gallon'
taken as written
taken as written
gin is a spirit
O looks like zero, nothing
G is the abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: Continuing 12 Down: a drinker getting bad-tempered over a drink of under a gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: OVER A GIN loses its O, then goes under A, with G for gallon below. 'Mean' here is arithmetic, not stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Averaging means calculating the arithmetic mean of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Stifles son and parents

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
mothers are parents

explanation.surface: A son and his parents both suppressing feelings, or a family that suffocates.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother is to suffocate or suppress, so stifles is a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Minor royal men somehow star in The Prince and the Showgirl

definitions.text: star in The Prince and the Showgirl

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unexplained route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lesser royals somehow get to play the lead in a film about a prince and a showgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the film's plot, a prince romancing a performer, which helps the anagram feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1957 film The Prince and the Showgirl starred Marilyn Monroe opposite Laurence Olivier.

clue.text: Rest of story out of order

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a falsehood
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: The rest of the story has been told in the wrong sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' suggests an anagram, but it gives a word meaning not working.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to recline and take a rest, so the phrase means rest as a verb.

clue.text: Collected wine outside European airport

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the wine goes around the other pieces

parts.note: red is red wine
E is the abbreviation for European
LAX is Los Angeles International Airport

explanation.surface: Someone picked up wine bought outside a European airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' reads as picked up but is the adjective meaning composed.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected person is calm and composed, so relaxed is an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Force opening of safety lock

indicators.note: the opening is the very beginning, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of safety
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Forcing open a safety lock.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is physical force or pressure applied to an object, as in engineering.

clue.text: Ridicule while cutting support

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing sits within it

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
as can mean while, at the same time that

explanation.surface: Mocking someone at the same moment as cutting their financial backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to make fun of someone playfully, so it is a verb synonym for ridicule.

clue.text: Most influential member of Norwegian band pens record

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the band holds the record inside

parts.note: a-ha are the Norwegian pop group of Take On Me
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: The leading member of a Norwegian band writes a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' suggests writing songs but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpha of a group is its dominant individual, as with the alpha male of a pack.

clue.text: Brief Liam Fox about going into hospital department for skin treatment

indicators.note: making something brief cuts it short, so the name loses its last letter
going into means entering, so the jumbled letters sit inside the department
about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ENT is ear, nose and throat
Liam without its last letter

explanation.surface: Briefing the politician Liam Fox as he heads to a hospital clinic for his skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Liam Fox is a British Conservative politician; 'brief' looks like a verb meaning to inform him.
explanation.definitionFit: An exfoliant is a product that removes dead cells from the surface of the skin.

clue.text: Telegraph to me containing manoeuvre taken by retreating regiment

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece wraps around the other
something taken by another is held by it, so the manoeuvre goes inside
retreating means going backwards, so the regiment is read the other way

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers of the British Army
a ploy is a tactical manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A setter noting that the newspaper sent them a message about a regiment's tactics in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: REME reversed gives EMER, which holds PLOY: EM(PLOY)ER. The setter works for the Telegraph, so to him it is the firm that pays him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph publishes the setter's puzzles, so from the setter's point of view it is the organisation paying wages.

clue.text: Discover Red Cross is inspired by church and duty

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the word is drawn inside the church
to dis-cover is to take off the covering, so only the inner letter stays

parts.note: the middle letter of red
a cross is the letter X
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finding out that the Red Cross is motivated by faith and a sense of obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' reads as the charity but splits: Red loses its outside, Cross is X.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a tax charged on goods such as alcohol, so it is a kind of duty.

clue.text: Do nothing as Midge Ure finally joins station

indicators.note: joins means attaches to, so these pieces are added after the station

parts.note: STA is a standard abbreviation for station
a midge is a small fly, like a gnat

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of Ure

explanation.surface: Midge Ure, the Ultravox singer, finally signs up with a radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: Midge Ure is a Scottish musician; the clue splits his name into an insect and a surname, and the station goes in front even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay inactive and make no progress, so it means to do nothing.

clue.text: More than one saw Bill Withers?

parts.note: an ad is a bill, a printed notice
to wither is to age, grow old

explanation.surface: Did several people spot the soul singer Bill Withers?
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Withers was the singer of Lean on Me; 'saw' looks like the past of see but is a noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a proverb or old saying, so several of them are adages.
